completed_scope: Each canonical staged OCI manifest/blob receives its own inspectable retrieval record, per-response validators/windows and parent validation receipt in the publication transaction.
Every proxy graph read and discovery checks individual member cache state as well as current grants, source precedence and policy. Expired members force bounded root revalidation.

Root 304 responses reuse verified exact root bytes but renew dependencies. Mutable manifests use strong ETags; weak/time-only validators force a full fetch. Unsolicited or contradictory 304s fail closed.

Internal request receipts admit successful zero-freshness fills without creating later cache hits. Stale receipts require classified temporary failure and each required member window; invalidation, negatives and active fetching remain fences.

Journal sequence ordering prevents older parent/tag/catalog work from erasing newer invalidation or conflicting tag state. Controlled tests set wall timestamps backward and preserve the durable ordering fence.

Stock ORAS tests prove direct/parent/catalog member revalidation, zero-freshness pull/tags/referrers and the earlier proxy/group workflows. All prior native npm/Python/OCI/Maven/generic journeys replayed.
The shared-digest native denial fixture now uses stock oras tag instead of two timestamp-sensitive pushes.

retained_failures.cause: Implicit graph members had no independently inspectable cache records.
An older tag fill could undo a newer catalog binding.
Two fixture pushes could create different manifests across timestamp boundaries; replaced with oras tag.
First setup used the previous binary embedded schema. Rebuilt/migrated before repeated passing database tests.
New contradictory-304 fixture initially returned 200 instead of exercising the intended condition. Corrected fixture; repeated database replay passed.
